artifacts.summary: Recommends a new one-page file context/standards/shared-worktree-discipline.md (rejecting git-safety.md and git-workflow-narrative.md as placement, with reasoning) and a short literal MUST-NOT bullet pointer in each of the 14 implementation agent definitions plus the agent template, mirroring the existing No-History-Rewrites bullet; confirms dependency task 356 is complete; re-derives the carried incident figures, confirming one and flagging two as unverifiable from this repository.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent system, an @-style entry in an implementation agent's own 'Context References' list does NOT reliably auto-resolve into a dispatched subagent's context -- it is read only if the agent actively chooses to open that path. For short, load-bearing, point-of-use guidance that must reach a subagent reliably, the working pattern (already used by general-implementation-agent.md's 'No History Rewrites' MUST NOT bullet) is a short literal MUST-NOT-style bullet directly in the agent's own Critical Requirements list, ending in a path citation to the full-detail standards file -- not a bare Context Reference entry, and not full duplication of the whole section.

When a new task's placement question for a short, discoverability-critical standards doc resembles an earlier one, check specs/archive/ for a precedent before surveying candidate files from scratch -- in this codebase, 'post-incident-verification-checklist' already surveyed git-safety.md, git-staging-scope.md, and git-workflow-narrative.md for near-identical shared-worktree-git-safety content and rejected all three as the wrong shape (safety-commit/rollback playbook; staging-scope contract; lazily-loaded reactive elaboration respectively), creating a new one-page file instead. That rejection reasoning transfers directly to adjacent placement questions in the same document family.
